typography_notes: Sans-serif throughout, likely Arial/Calibri. Title is bold red and larger than all other text. Label boxes use white bold text on solid blue or red fills. Table headers and row labels are bold blue; the y row values are blue; most numeric cell values are black. Subscript-style labels such as X1, X2, x1 are written with the number immediately after the letter. The question text is blue inside a blue-outlined white box.

recreation_brief:
1. Use a 16:9 white slide. Add the title textbox near the top-left: Effect of Overfitting on model parameter “W” in bold red sans-serif. Add a small yellow oval at the top-right containing 12 in black text.
2. On the left, add four filled label boxes with white bold text: blue “Training Data”; red “Perfect Data” with a second line “Y follows x1”; red “x8 is Outlier”; red “x8 is Outlier”.
3. Add the first center table as 4 rows x 9 columns. Header row: blank, X1, X2, X3, X4, X5, X6, X7, X8. Row X1: 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 11. Row X2: 1, 3, 5, 6, 16, 7, 5, 3. Row y: 2, 4, 6, 8, 16, 18, 20, 22. Use blue bold headers/row labels, black numeric values, and blue y-row values.
4. Add the Test Data block at the top-right: blue label “Test Data”, then a 4 rows x 4 columns table. Header: blank, Test1, Test2, Test3. Row X1: 30, 40, 50. Row X2: 15, 20, 25. Row y: 60, 80, 100.
5. Add the middle outlier table with the same layout as the first table, but set the last cell in row X1 to 30 and fill that cell yellow.
6. Add the red callout to the right of the middle table with two lines: Again / Y follows x1. Add a red curved arrow from this callout pointing left toward the middle table.
7. Add the bottom outlier table with the same layout as the first table, but set the last cell in row X1 to 60 and fill that cell yellow.
8. Add the bottom-right question box: white fill, blue border, blue text: What will be the effect of X8 Outlier values on the trained model ???
